It would also hand NIL to HANDLER from a nonblocking socket-accept. io.lisp:7609-7610 (fnn-recover-log docstring): "then the five recovery barriers the per-file open runs", but fnn-store-recovery-barriers (7217-7229) returns three thunks, and its own docstring cites *fn-sf-recovery-barrier-count* 3.
fix: Delete the second lstat check and fnn-accept-any-loop. Change the fnn-recover-log docstring to the three barriers fnn-store-recovery-barriers runs.
notes: 10-02 23:05 fixed; ran tests.test_native_build_scripts (3 new red->green); io.lisp not recompiled
reviewer: All three points are confirmed, and none is a runtime failure. The store-exists check appears twice in a row (io.lisp:4567-4570). fnn-accept-any-loop (5761-5769) has no callers in host/, tests/ or tools/. It and fnn-accept-loop (5719-5723) would also pass a NIL accept result to HANDLER, though bp-control.lisp:163 and :191 follow the same raw socket-accept pattern and those are live. fnn-recover-log's docstring says "the five recovery barriers" (7609-7610), but fnn-store-recovery-barriers returns three thunks and cites *fn-sf-recovery-barrier-count* 3 (7217-7229).
scenario: No runtime failure from the duplicate check. The dead accept loop is a hazard for whoever revives it (the NIL accept described in the first finding). The docstring's barrier count disagrees with the code and with the three-barrier theorem it cites, which misleads a reader auditing crash cuts.
title: Duplicated store-exists check in import, dead fnn-accept-any-loop, and a docstring that says five recovery barriers where the code has three
